title: Quantification and Phenotyping of SARS-CoV-2-specific T Cell Response via Flow Cytometry
author: Mutavhatsindi, Riou
materials: BV421™ mouse anti-human Granzyme B antibody
Alexa Fluor® 700 mouse anti-human IFN-γ antibody
Fresh blood collected in Sodium Heparin tubes
D-PBS liquid w/o Ca and Mg

steps.title: Check cytometer configuration
steps.instruction: Verify that the flow cytometer settings and laser configuration are compatible with the 11‑color SARS‑CoV‑2 T‑cell panel before starting the assay.

steps.title: Prepare antibody master mix
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube combine the following reagents in the order shown: 10 µL BD Brilliant Stain Buffer Plus, 220 µL 1× eBioscience Permeabilization solution (q.s. 50 µL), then the fluorophore‑conjugated antibodies listed in Table 2 (volumes per stain and total for 20 stains + 10 % overage: IFN‑γ Alexa 700 0.2 µL (4.4 µL), Granzyme‑B BV421 0.3 µL (6.6 µL), TNF‑α FITC 0.4 µL (8.8 µL), PD‑1 PE 0.5 µL (11.0 µL), CD45RA BV605 0.5 µL (11.0 µL), CD4 PE‑Cy7 0.5 µL (11.0 µL), CD3 BV785 0.6 µL (13.2 µL), IL‑2 PE/Dazzle 594 0.7 µL (15.4 µL), Perforin APC 0.9 µL (19.8 µL), CD27 PE‑Cy5 1.0 µL (22.0 µL), CD8 BV510 1.3 µL (28.6 µL)). Keep all reagents on ice during preparation.

steps.title: Vortex and centrifuge antibody mix
steps.instruction: Vortex the antibody master mix briefly, then centrifuge at 12 000 rpm (≈8 500 rcf) for 4 min in a mini‑centrifuge. Store the cleared mix at 4 °C in the dark until use.

steps.title: Add antibody mix to samples
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the prepared antibody mix to each well containing stimulated whole‑blood, pipette up‑and‑down 8–10 times (avoid bubbles), and incubate 45 min at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: First permeabilization wash
steps.instruction: Add 170 µL of 1× eBioscience Permeabilization solution to each well, then centrifuge at 500 × g for 4 min at room temperature. Discard the supernatant by flicking the plate (invert over waste and tap on a paper towel).

steps.title: Second permeabilization wash
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 1× eBioscience Permeabilization solution, mix by pipetting up‑and‑down 8–10 times, centrifuge at 500 × g for 4 min at room temperature, and discard the supernatant by flicking the plate.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 1 % formaldehyde solution, mix 8–10 times, and incubate 15 min at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Final wash and resuspend
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL PBS, centrifuge at 500 × g for 4 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, then resuspend the cell pellet in 160 µL PBS. Transfer the suspension to pre‑labeled microtiter tubes and store at 4 °C protected from light until acquisition.

steps.title: Prepare compensation control tubes
steps.instruction: Label 14 × 5 mL polystyrene tubes as shown in Figure 4. To each tube add 100 µL 1× eBioscience Permeabilization solution, then 15 µL anti‑Rat or anti‑Mouse Ig compensation beads (as appropriate), followed by 1 µL of the corresponding fluorochrome‑conjugated antibody.

steps.title: Stain and fix compensation beads
steps.instruction: Vortex the tubes gently and incubate 10 min at room temperature in the dark. Add 2 mL PBS containing 2 % FBS, vortex, then centrifuge at 500 g for 10 min at room temperature. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellets in 200 µL 1 % formaldehyde solution, incubate 15 min, add 2 mL PBS, vortex, centrifuge again at 500 g for 10 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, and finally resuspend each pellet in 200 µL PBS + 2 % FBS. Keep the compensation controls at 4 °C protected from light until use.

steps.title: Optional pause point for stained cells
steps.instruction: If immediate acquisition is not possible, store the stained cells at 4 °C protected from light for up to 16–20 h.

steps.title: Acquire data on flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Run the stained samples and compensation controls on a calibrated flow cytometer using the instrument settings verified in step 1.

steps.title: Analyze flow data
steps.instruction: Import the FCS files into FlowJo v10.7.1, apply the gating strategy (Figure 5) to identify CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells, and quantify IFN‑γ, TNF‑α, and IL‑2 expression. Define a positive response as a cytokine frequency at least two‑fold above the unstimulated background and subtract background values. For phenotyping, include only events with ≥30 antigen‑specific cells. Visualize and perform statistical analysis in GraphPad Prism v9.1.0.

description: This protocol provides reagents and specific steps for quantifying and immunophenotyping the SARS-CoV-2 spike-specific T-cell response from whole blood samples. Here, we present an 11-color antibody panel designed to identify IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-2 production, memory differentiation markers (CD45RA and CD27), cytotoxic molecules (Granzyme-B and Perforin), and the inhibitory receptor, PD-1. Furthermore, blood stimulation can be performed with peptide pools from other pathogens (examples are given in this protocol using a Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) specific-peptide pool). For the cell staining steps, other antibodies targeting different markers of interest can be included. Before starting, it is essential to check the configuration of your instrument to ensure compatibility with the reagents used in the proposed panel.
